body: This change flips the logic, and it has nothing to do with the rest of the PR. The old code set `slug` only when team billing was **disabled** and `requestedSlug` only when it was **enabled**. With this change, a self-hosted instance (billing off) creates organizations with no slug at all, and a billing-enabled instance sets the slug right away, skipping the requestedSlug/payment flow. Revert to `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`.

Null dereference. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError whenever the location is Google Meet. The old code used `?.` and fell back to Cal Video. Every Google Meet booking by a user with no destination calendar now fails. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Video/non-calendar references used to get `credentialId: result.credentialId`. Now they always get `undefined`, so booking references for Zoom/Daily/etc. lose their credentialId. Later updates and deletes of the video meeting look up the credential by `reference.credentialId` and will now fail or pick the wrong one. Keep `result.credentialId` for both branches.

In this fallback branch (destination has no credentialId), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without an externalId. The resulting reference is then saved with `externalCalendarId: undefined`, because `create()` now reads `result.externalId` instead of `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updates and deletes then have no calendar id (see the Google update/delete comments), so rescheduling and cancelling break for these destinations. Pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

Only GoogleCalendarService uses the new `credentialId` argument to pick the right destination calendar. Office365, Lark and CalDAV (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`) still take `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the organizer's calendar. In a collective event where a second host uses Office365 or CalDAV, the host's own credential tries to write into the organizer's calendar id: you get a 404/403, or for CalDAV the filter matches no calendar and nothing is created. The `externalId` for this destination is already passed to `createEvent`, so it should go to the calendar service (e.g. a new calendar-id argument) rather than just being echoed back in the result.

Regression: the calendar is now picked only by matching `credentialId`. A destination calendar with `credentialId == null` (legacy rows, or the integration-only fallback path in `createAllCalendarEvents`) used to go to `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now it silently goes to `primary`, the wrong calendar. Fall back to the main destination's externalId when no credential match is found.

This fallback can never match. It only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and then it looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. `=== undefined/null/""`). The result is always `undefined`, so `calendars.events.update` gets `calendarId: undefined` and the Google API call fails. The old code fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Match on credentialId, or fall back to the first destination calendar or `primary`.

Same bug as in `updateEvent`: the `find` compares against the falsy `externalCalendarId`, so it never matches and always falls through to `primary`. Events that were created in a non-primary destination calendar (for example through the reference path that now drops externalCalendarId) won't be deleted.

If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, this is `null`. The `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` below then does nothing, so the other collective hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped. That is exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. Initialise to `[]`, or assign `[...(base ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

When the event type has its own `destinationCalendar` (a team-level calendar that belongs to the organizer's credential), you still append every other host's destination calendar. There's no dedup, so if two hosts point to the same calendar or credential, duplicate events get created. The Booking row also stores only `destinationCalendar[0]` (see the `connect` below). Flows that rebuild `evt` from the booking (cancel, confirm, payment webhooks, requestReschedule, editLocation, deleteCredential) therefore see only the organizer's calendar, and secondary hosts are left out of those operations (e.g. confirming a requires-confirmation booking creates the event only for the organizer).

The rewrite of `loadUsers` goes beyond the scope of this PR and changes behaviour. (1) The `organization: { select: { slug } }` selection for dynamic users was removed, but `IsFixedAwareUser` still declares `organization`. (2) Any error, including this plain `Error` and real Prisma errors other than `PrismaClientKnownRequestError`, gets turned into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" that hides the cause. Invalid input such as an empty dynamic user list should be a 4xx.

The credential for another host is loaded from the DB by `destination.credentialId`, sequentially, once per destination. Nothing checks that the credential belongs to a user who is actually a host of this booking, or that it isn't `invalid`. The same inline block is copy-pasted in `updateAllCalendarEvents`, and a variant is in handleCancelBooking. Consider a single batched `findMany` for all needed credential ids, a shared helper, and an ownership/`invalid` check.

If the credential is not in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup returns nothing (credential deleted, or no app slug), `credential` is `undefined` but is still passed to `updateEvent`, which will throw on `credential.appName`/`getCalendar`. Skip the reference, or push a failed result, when no credential is found. Separately, the `newBookingId` merge path below still deletes only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`), so the other hosts' old events are orphaned when bookings are merged.

The recurring-series branch now runs once per calendar reference. Each time, it loops over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and all `updatedBookings` using only the first `_calendar` ref (`find`). With N references, the same organizer events get N redundant delete calls, and the other hosts' events for the remaining occurrences are never deleted, because their references and credentials are never used here. Also note that the credential fetched from the DB above is only used in the non-recurring branch.
